name: AP Japanese Language and Culture
overview: AP Japanese Language and Culture develops interpretive, interpersonal, and presentational communication in Japanese, organized around six themes and the cultures of Japan and Japanese-speaking communities. Students read and write in hiragana, katakana, and kanji and use appropriate levels of politeness. The course and exam were revised for 2026-27: students complete a research project during the year that feeds into the spoken part of the exam, and the written tasks are a story narration and an email response.
examMode: Fully digital in Bluebook from May 2027 (spoken responses recorded and written responses typed in the app)

sections.name: Section I, Question 1
sections.notes: 3 minutes to prepare and 3 minutes to present what you learned from your research project.

sections.name: Section I, Question 2
sections.notes: Four pre-recorded questions about your project; 40 seconds to answer each.

sections.name: Section I, Question 3
sections.notes: Write a story based on a series of four pictures. Questions 3 and 4 share 30 minutes.

sections.name: Section I, Question 4
sections.notes: Reply to an email from a friend or community member.

sections.name: Section II, Part A
sections.notes: Questions on audio such as conversations, announcements, and reports.

sections.name: Section II, Part B
sections.notes: Questions on texts such as notes, ads, articles, emails, and stories.

skills.name: Interpretive communication
skills.description: Understand main ideas, details, purpose, and audience in written and audio texts.

skills.name: Interpersonal communication
skills.description: Respond spontaneously and appropriately to questions.

skills.name: Presentational communication
skills.description: Present information and arguments in organized speech and writing.

skills.name: Cultural comparison
skills.description: Connect products, practices, and perspectives of Japanese-speaking communities to your own.

scoring.summary: Multiple choice (listening 25%, reading 25%) is half the score; the project presentation (20%), project Q&A (15%), story narration (7.5%), and email response (7.5%) are the other half. Free responses are scored holistically on task completion, organization, language use, and register. Klutch's practice tasks use simplified practice scales.

frqTypes.name: Project presentation
frqTypes.howScored: Klutch practice scale (holistic, 0–5): clear, organized presentation of research findings with cultural content and comparison, fluent delivery, and accurate language.

frqTypes.name: Project Q&A
frqTypes.howScored: Klutch practice scale (1 point per answer): each answer responds directly, elaborates, and uses appropriate register.

frqTypes.name: Story narration
frqTypes.howScored: Klutch practice scale (holistic, 0–5): a complete, logical story covering all four pictures, with transitions, varied vocabulary and structures, and accurate kana and kanji.

frqTypes.name: Email response
frqTypes.howScored: Klutch practice scale (holistic, 0–5): answers every question in the email, elaborates, uses appropriate register and email conventions, and accurate language.

strategy: Read the questions before each audio or text so you know what to look for.
In story narration, cover every picture in order and connect events with まず, それから, ところが, そのあと, 結局.
In the email response, answer every question and match the politeness level (です・ます with teachers and community members).
Use a range of structures: ～ので, ～のに, ～ても, ～たら, ～ために, ～ようにする, passive and causative forms.
For the Q&A, answer in the first sentence, then give a reason and an example; fill the 40 seconds.
Rehearse your project presentation so you can deliver it from your outline without reading.
pitfalls: Choosing the wrong kanji when converting typed kana.
Mixing plain and polite forms in the same email.
Skipping one of the four pictures in story narration.
Using casual speech with a teacher or community member.
Confusing は and が, or に and で, in key sentences.

caveats: The course and exam were revised for 2026-27; details of the project and scoring guidelines may still be updated. Check AP Central.
Klutch cannot play audio; listening practice uses written transcripts labeled as audio sources.
Klutch's practice texts use standard kanji without furigana; vocabulary lists give readings.
All passages and transcripts are original and written by Klutch.
